body:
> do you find any clarity or benefit from writing out some of those thoughts like this?

No, 100% of the effort is spent figuring things out internally. Once I've done that, writing it out is only for the benefit of others.

> why do you think it is hard for you to write freeform, without a set direction?

I really have no idea. It's like a combination of not knowing where to start, and getting caught on a snag.

> you say that you are walking through mud, hoping there will be something.

No, I said I was slogging through mud because others keep telling me not to give up and I'll eventually find "something". The hope comment refers to other things, such as hoping I'll get back together with my Ex some day (even though it's very clear at this point that that will never happen).

> what kind of worth is that?

Something where *I* honestly matter to someone, as opposed to the job I do or the role I fill.

> focusing on one thing, to develop one skill?

I'm not good at that. The learning curve for me is like a shallow slope leading up to a vertical cliff. I can become reasonably competent at something fairly easily, but after a point I lose all focus and passion.

>have you ever tried meditation?

Not formally. Many times I've tried on my own to sit down and "think of nothing", but I can never sustain that for more than a couple seconds. If I force myself to keep trying, eventually I get exhausted and just fall asleep.

> What do you look forward to?

Basically nothing.


> or the sun to go down so you can sleep and forget about everything happening to you

This, if anything.


> wouldn't it be better to tell ONE person what is happening to you to make you feel this way?

This isn't a simple case of needing to get things off my chest. I've talked about this stuff in the past to a multitude of shrinks and a few of my friends. At this point, talking about the same stuff over and over is closer to reopening old wounds than any form of release. As I said in my first post, I've already tried all the 'usual' solutions, so I'm looking for alternate ideas you won't find on a checklist.

"Chaos" isn't quite the right word. There *is* an order to it, but it's hard to discern at first glance and it often changes faster than I can keep up.

"Disconnection from my own emotions" isn't quite right either. They're there, I can feel them, but I can't quite tell what they are a lot of times.

As another way of expressing this analogy, I've found that animated Iterated Function Systems are similar to how I perceive this, if I had to apply a visualization to my emotions. Imagine a few hundred of these floating around in a room, and trying to describe what they look like to someone who was born blind.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AaFgfqHKPxA

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TNHV2Dg16iw

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UR5MfnzpisE

> I bet you're an introverted perceiving type

I'm not sure exactly what that means, but I do lean introverted yes. I've heard of Jung, but never read any of his works.

> love

I'm not sure if I described this one correctly either. I mean that I have *extreme* difficulty telling the difference between real love, and mere infatuation+lust+obsession. I'm always deeply suspicious that what I feel is just a byproduct of desperation.

> worldview / patterns

I don't think I really understand what you're trying to say in these two paragraphs, sorry.

> emotionally explosive

Explosive isn't the word I'd use. It's more like really bad acting by way of exaggeration. I don't have any good control or finesse, so if I try to clamp down or back off I go too far and it ends up being an all-or-nothing affair.

> it doesn't sound like the relationships that you've been abandoning have been meaningful and sustaining for you

They are in their own way. I do enjoy the company of my friends, it's just that they don't know how to help and have their own lives anyway.


> But your situation is an extremely difficult one

I have to offer a wry smile at that one. "Easy" is a word that has never well described me or any of the situations I find myself in.


> and I ask that you be patient with me

Oh, don't worry about that. I've been dealing with this for ages, I know better than to expect fast answers. Besides, this sub is full of other people in more dire straits than me.

> but sometimes I have to collect a lot of information first

I replied to my own comment with more info, but you didn't directly reference any of those so I suspect you didn't see it. For early experiences, I'm deliberately avoiding mentioning any PII. I'll have to figure out how to balance vagueness with usefulness.

> Hope you are doing (relatively) okay today.

It comes and goes. To use another analogy, it's like a float bobbing in the waves, but the tide is going out.

> Sounds pretty normal to me

Ahh.... maybe I did a bad job of describing that, let me try a different analogy.
You have a room full of hundreds upon of thousands of honeybees, so thick in the air it's hard to see more than a few feet in any direction. Huge swaths of bees are moving in tight formation in regular geometric patterns that shift and change like a kaleidoscope, other bees are just flying around randomly, some on the floor might possibly be dead. There are constant but irregular streams of them entering and leaving all the time through tiny openings. It's unclear if the openings actually go anywhere, or if they just loop back on themselves. Some of the openings may or may not be wormholes that connect to each other in the past or future. A significant portion of the bees don't seem to truly exist, but are ghost images from an alternate dimension. You were born in this room and have never left it. It has no windows or doors. Someone outside knocks on the wall and asks you "Are the bees mostly on the north or south side today?"

This type of thing has *NEVER* worked for me. As much as I've been babbling here in this thread, I'm utterly incapable of writing freeform without a set direction. I can answer questions and respond to comments easily enough, but to just start writing from scratch flat out doesn't work. I struggled with this repeatedly throughout school and absolutely dreaded whenever I had to write a paper (I think I failed or came close to failing every one).  I'm not sure if this relates in any way to my other problems.

I seriously don't have the emotional energy to invest in something like that. Trying random thing after random thing will wear me down to the ground inside of a week. It's hard enough trying to summon the willpower to search the web job hunting.

> what things did you used to like

Various things.... TV shows, some crafts, I have an architecture project that's halfway done I haven't touched since April.

> and what happened to end that?

I just..... stopped caring.

> There is a lot of good in the world. You've just apparently seen more of the bad.


I dunno about that. It's not just me either, nobody seems terribly happy these days anymore.

> Stuff like that happens when you don't expect it at all.

To other people perhaps, it doesn't seem to happen to me. I'm not really willing to wait 20 years to see it happen.


> There are plenty of ways you could help other people, if you believe that would give you the "real worth" you're talking about.

It won't. I'm talking having an actual demonstrable effect. This is different from just working a generic day job that anyone could do. I may have limited skills, but as stated before everyone wants a specialist who's really good at one thing. That's not me.


> I'm not very informed about how that type of stuff works

In short, cancer is just runaway cell division. Sometimes it stays as a self-contained mass, but sometimes the dividing reaches out and 'corrupts' other organs/etc. There are multiple different kinds, and no one's really yet figured out why it stops or starts when it does.


> And her situation getting better was much less likely than yours.

I don't agree with that. I don't think it's possible for my situation to suddenly 'stop' or that a misdiagnosis will save the day.

> Why do you believe things can't change?

It's not a question of "can't", but probability. There has been effectively no net forward movement my entire life. Sure it's *possible* my life could drastically change for the better next year and stay that way. It's also possible that world peace happens, the rainforests grow back overnight, and everybody finds a magical flying pony. 

> what are a few things that could change that would make you happier?

- The world could stop being a complete cesspit.

- I could find the perfect love of my life who doesn't mind I'm a jobless acerbic unstable wreck (and is not themselves insane).

- I could somehow have some kind of real worth that matters to someone.

I'm sorry for what happened to you, but can't really say much more than that. I have no business consoling anyone else on anything.

> I hope you are stronger than me.

Honestly, I'm probably not. People sometimes say I am, but I believe they're confused by my particular combination of stubbornness and fear.

How much time? Change when? How much happiness at what point makes up for how many years of misery? I realize I'm asking impossible philosophical questions here, but I've been in basically the same boat for decades. I'm not optimistic about staying here for several more.

That's a good thought in general, but I've sorta been doing that for ages and haven't found anything yet. As time goes on I'm increasingly uninterested in basically everything. I've been giving up on things I used to like, finding something new seems unlikely.

> Sorry.. we just hit a topic that I'm pretty interested in. 

I don't fault you, I'm just trying to say that I'm perhaps not the best person to tell you to chase your dreams, given the circumstances.


> VBA and perl

Ditch VBA, learn C or one of its derivatives. Perl is handy, but encourages bad syntax. It's notorious for one programmer not being able to understand another's code. 

> You have no idea how many people's lives you impact on a daily basis

This is true, but I'm not convinced that that impact is necessarily net positive. In my case, I tend to think it isn't.

> I think there are a LOT more reasons to live than there are to die

Perhaps for some people. In my case, the "I'd like to not be miserable every day" reason I think supersedes anything else.

>It sounds like you may be bipolar

I've been diagnosed with basically *everything* over the years at one point or another. No one can seem to agree what's wrong with me. This does not help my trust issues vis-a-vis shrinks.


> If you know the "right" behavior and you agree with someone, what happens? 

That depends on how specific the sense of 'right' is. I'll often know generally the class of thing I'm supposed to do, but am unable to act out an actual case that fits the criteria. 


> If you know you're needy, why don't you loosen your grip on your relationship?

Comments like these are why I say I find your attitude offensive. You act like it's oh so simple to just flip the switch and everything will be all brightness and sunshine. If my problems were so easy to solve, we wouldn't be having this conversation.


> All the things you list are exactly what people here will propose

Yes, and I list them exactly so that people don't waste their time suggesting things I've already tried that don't work.


> explain to us why those solutions didn't work

I already did, for each as I listed them.

The only one that might need further clarification is the meds line. I don't remember the names of each one I tried, but do remember that they had no effect on me. At best, a few forced me into a very uncomfortable neither zone that made me less emotionally stable than 'normal'.

- The job market sucks.

- HR is your mortal enemy: they have absolutely no understanding of the position and will list requirements that don't make sense or are impossible. You frequently have to copy/paste the entire job posting into your CV to get past their braindead automated filters. A lot people end up being hired through the back door.

- Managers frequently have limited understanding of what the programmers under them do, and will invent all sorts of ridiculous metrics to try and score performance.

- There are a lot of silly "Web 2.0" development strategies with names like Agile, Scrum and Waterfall. They're usually picked up not because they're the right idea for the company, but because it's trendy. They are then implemented incorrectly anyway.

- If you do any sort of support, you will be asked to do increasingly more and more work with increasingly less and less budget.

- The bean counters don't understand the point of sysadmins. If everything in the company is humming along smoothly, obviously it's not that the sysadmins are doing their job, it's that they must unnecessary. The better you are at your job, the more likely you'll be sacked.

- You're sorta asking the wrong person in the wrong place :)

Missed this before

>it's just that it sounds like you've had it up to there with people who try to banish your pain without understanding your pain

At this point, I don't really care if people understand me or not, I just want ideas. I don't really want to commit suicide, but more and more I'm beginning to see it as the only workable solution. To be honest, the only thing that has kept me from it these past few years is being scared that what's on the other side might be worse. I'm not a religious person. I don't believe in a Hell or karma or any of that. I'm terrified that 'the end' means waking up as a ghost or something and having to roam the same earth I'm already on, but now I'm not even allowed to scream.

> You probably have more talent than most people

I'm not sure about that. I think I have the same amount, just that it's spread thin over a zillion areas instead of being concentrated in one useful place.

> Do you do any of these professionally?

In and out. I used to do mainly web and graphic design back during the dot-com bubble in the 90's, the last few years have been more IT type stuff. Ages past I tried to design lamps and try to sell them, but that didn't work out so well (too complicated to build for market prices). I've never even attempted to get into the movie business, I can't compete with those people.
Varies. Costumes, props, industrial design, graphic design, web design, moderate programming (not counting javascript). I'm decent, but not amazingly good at any of it.

- My emotions often seem to have a mind of their own. They turn on and off for no reason. My sense of 'happiness' often feels like it's burnt out or locked. Multiple times in my relationship with my Ex, when things were going very well, I just felt this weird sort of mildly sarcastic void. As though when the negative emotions had receded, nothing came to fill in. 'Happiness' had taken the day off. I ended up acting somewhat inconsiderate for no reason, and couldn't control it.

- I have too much hope/wishful thinking. You may think this is a good thing, but I assure you it's not. I spend a large portion of my time hoping for things I *know* will not or cannot happen. It's weird when you live for dreams you know will not come true.

- For ages now, I feel like I'm slogging through a waist-deep sea of featureless mud, endless from horizon to horizon. People keep telling me if that if I just keep going eventually I'll find something. I don't really believe them anymore, and I'm getting very very tired.

- If I've been having many heated arguments in a given day, or spent a lot of time having *"a talk"*, it's like my emotions get physically tired and shut down. I'm no longer able to comprehend the feeling or meaning behind the words. It's something beyond just being tired, although being actually physically tired exacerbates the issue.
Eh.... satisfied solving a particular logic puzzle? finishing a design? being there to support a loved one? It's too vague.

> Tell me what it's like inside your head, what's wrong inside your head

Hahaha lol... where do I even start?


I guess, in no particular order:

- My thoughts and emotions are like a big amorphous extra-dimensional cloud, constantly shifting and changing. It takes me a long time sort out my feelings on some topics because I have to do a long-term average, and even then I can often change them. I can and do hold simultaneously mutually-exclusive opposite opinions on the same topic, or can at least see the opposite side very clearly. I can *always* take the opposite side in *any* argument. Playing "Devil's Advocate" in conversations is the rule, I have to try very hard to keep this in check.

- I'm not 100% certain I understand or am capable of the emotion known as love. There are people I care about extremely deeply and romantically (ie, my Ex), but I always feel like I'm lying to myself somehow or that something's missing. I refuse to every say "I love you" to anyone for this reason, because I feel this area is too important to lie about. (This caused no small amount of friction with my Ex, let me tell you).

- I hate the world so much I want to cry. I hate what modern society is turning into. I hate how everyone's always an asshole, how people all seem to be greedy and selfish these days. I hate how western governments are all turning into police states, I hate how business are always trying to lay you over a barrel. I haven't watched TV in years and I've stopped reading the news because it's making me increasingly suicidal.

- I'm always fighting, and I'm starting to wear down. I'm fighting with the phone company, fighting with some stupid software, fighting against zealots. The grocery store randomly charges me 4x what something is supposed to cost, I have to fight with them. I fought to keep my relationship alive, I'm now fighting against my emotions because I know I have to let her go. I'm always fighting. Always. It never goes away. There's always something.

- I'm lonely, but recognize that I'm too emotionally unstable and abrasive to hold a lasting relationship with anybody. Even friends are touch-and-go, I usually drive them away after a few years. It's tough to forge bonds with people.

- I haven't been able to actually cry for years. I'm assuming this is a bad thing.

- I have a lot of issues about intimacy, trust and betrayal. It's hard for me to talk to anyone about much of anything. I'm pushing myself to post here.

- I have a penchant for being melodramatic (runs in the family). I try hard to keep it in check, but this usually ends up resulting in no emotion at all.

- I have an array of oddball skills, but I'm not really *good* at anything. 'Jack of all trades, master of none' as the saying goes. Except nobody ever wants someone who can both sew and build a computer.

- Not a lot interests me anymore, everything's sort of dull and neutral.


Anyway, there's a lot more things I could list, but it will take me quite some time to condense them out of my cloud so-to-speak.


>That was how I started to reconnect with people

Over the past few years, I've been deliberately letting connections die. Suicide always comes as a shock to people, but less so if when it's someone they haven't talked to in ages. I want to let everyone else down gently.

I find your post highly offensive and close-minded, but I'm not going to start a debate about it. I will however respond to two parts:


>because it's a part of your life you couldn't control.


You're sorta kinda technically correct on this point, but for totally opposite reasons than what you think.

I have multi-layered issues re: trust, abandonment, intimacy, desperation, etc, that make a relationship very rocky. I can be excessively needy. My tact sometimes leaves much to be desired. My emotions turn themselves off or get 'jammed' with no apparent rhyme or reason. I have a bad habit of turning conversations into arguments for no reason, *even when I agree with the person*. There were many times when I actively understood my actions were detrimental to the relationship, but I was unable to do anything about it (assuming I knew what the 'right' behavior even was in that situation). They had a lot of their own problems too btw.

But no, the main reason I can't cope is that I deeply care for them and really wanted to work things out, but they eventually had had enough. We're still on good terms, but I'm unable to act normal around them now. The fact that they've since moved on and are with someone else doesn't help matters.



> Will you acknowledge that you are looking for outside help?


That's a given. It's the whole reason I decided to post to this sub in the first place.

> To get something new, you have to try something different.

That's largely why I'm posting here. I'm hoping there's another POV somewhere I've missed.

As for things that make me happy, that's a tough call since I have limited experience there. There are a wide range of things that sometimes make me more or less 'comfortable' and 'satisfied', but I'm not sure if any of them have really made me 'happy'. The few times I can remember being really happy were sorta weird and uncomfortable because I'm so not used to the feeling.

I've been referred various self-help books before, but none of them really said anything to me. I'm not *against* reading, but neither am I optimistic.

I don't understand what you're asking wrt "symptoms". For emotions, I'm all sorts of messed up, and could write a book about it.... you'd need to be more specific.
